steps.path: Every comment and reply, in the panel and the hover card
steps.headline: Where should Edit and Delete live on a comment?
steps.today: Once a comment or reply is posted it can only be resolved. There is no way to fix a typo or remove one.
steps.problem: A typo, a wrong comment, or a leftover test comment stays forever.
steps.proposal: Each comment and each reply gets Edit and Delete.

options.label: A ⋯ menu
pros: Same as Google Docs and Word
Room to add more actions later
cons: One extra click to reach Edit or Delete
On the phone the ⋯ must always show, since there is no hover

options.label: Small icons on hover
cons: Two more icons on every card and reply
Easy to hit Delete by accident beside Resolve

steps.headline: Whose comments can you edit or delete?
steps.today: Comments come from you, the assistant, and — in Word or Excel files — colleagues who commented in Word or Excel.
steps.problem: Letting you delete anyone's note is handy but can wipe a colleague's comment from a shared file.

options.label: Yours and the assistant's
pros: You can clean up anything the assistant wrote
A colleague's comment in a shared Word or Excel file can't be wiped by mistake
cons: To remove a colleague's comment you'd resolve it, or delete it in Word or Excel

options.label: Only your own
cons: You couldn't delete a comment the assistant made by mistake

options.label: Anyone's
pros: Same as Word and Excel, which let you delete anyone's comment
cons: Easy to delete a colleague's note in a file you'll send back to them

steps.path: Deleting the first comment of a thread that has replies
steps.headline: Deleting a thread's first comment — what happens to its replies?
steps.today: A thread is the first comment plus its replies.
steps.problem: Replies make no sense without the comment they answer.
steps.proposal: Pick what deleting the first comment does.

options.label: Deletes the whole thread
pros: Same as Google Docs, Word and Excel
cons: Removes replies you might have wanted — the confirmation below says how many

options.label: Keeps replies, marks it deleted
cons: A "deleted comment" stub stays in the thread
Word and Excel have no such state, so in those files the whole thread still goes

steps.headline: Should deleting ask first?
steps.problem: A mis-click could remove a comment for good — in Word and Excel files it's removed from the file itself.

options.label: Delete now, offer Undo
cons: If you miss the Undo, it's gone
For Word and Excel, undo means rewriting the file a second time

steps.headline: Should an edited comment say it was edited?
steps.today: Comments show who wrote them and when.
steps.problem: Without a mark, someone replying to the old wording can look confusing.
steps.proposal: A small muted "edited" after the time, like Google Docs and Slack. Word and Excel files don't record edits, so it would only show on other files — and only for edits made in YouCoded.

steps.headline: Should the assistant be able to edit or delete comments?
steps.today: The assistant can read, reply, resolve, reopen, add and move comments — not edit or delete them.
steps.problem: Letting it edit or delete means it could change or remove what people wrote.
steps.proposal: Pick what the assistant may do.

options.label: Neither
pros: It can never change or remove what anyone wrote
It can still resolve, which hides without losing anything
cons: To fix its own typo it replies again instead

options.label: Only its own
pros: It can tidy up its own mistakes
cons: Two more tools for it to learn
Word and Excel changes would ask permission, as today
